children: Norges Bank raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 4.5% in September 2026, in line with market expectations, as policymakers stepped up efforts to curb inflation.
CPI inflation picked up to 3.3% in August, the highest in four months, while underlying inflation also rose to 3%.
The US-Iran war continues to cloud the price outlook, with rising oil and gas prices, as well as higher prices for several other raw materials.

The central bank signaled that the policy rate will likely need to remain elevated for some time and said it is prepared to tighten policy further if necessary to bring inflation back to its 2% target within a reasonable period.
At the same time, economic activity increased broadly as expected, while employment continued to rise and unemployment remained largely unchanged in recent months.
Meanwhile, capacity utilization appears to have declined slightly less than previously estimated in June.

title: Norges Bank Raises Policy Rate to 4.5% as Expected
